deckType: Writing Craft / Character Psychology / Honesty vs. Fidelity
bundleSuggestion: Strong pairing with Story Masters, Writers Room, Storytelling Masterclass

cards.power: Surface Tension. Deflect 1 attack using "Traits." Opponent must address your haircut instead of your core.
cards.lore: The psychic economy of the character. The traits, the green shirt, the tan insignia — a delicate shell hiding the rot inside.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanic and metaphor are one — deflect with surface, hide the rot.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: split face mask, smooth exterior / rotten interior. Mood: unsettling calm.

cards.power: Subconscious Betrayal. Force opponent to reveal a card.
cards.lore: Why do you hold your hand like that? To set people at ease? Or to hide the shaking? Multiple humans use the same crutch.
cards.gradeReason: Body language as forced reveal — you know the betrayal immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: hand gripping syringe, other hand trembling behind back. Mood: nervous concealment.

cards.power: Value Nuke. Destroy all "Trait" cards in play.
cards.lore: Honesty. Fidelity. Interconnection. The reason you can't have both the money and the girl.
cards.gradeReason: Nuke all surfaces to reveal core values — the deck's entire thesis in one move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: ribcage opened, glowing VALUES gem inside. Mood: raw exposure.

cards.power: Tear Gas. All players skip 1 turn remembering Their "Glowing Core."
cards.lore: Push them to the wall. Peel back the layers — the smiles, the costumes — until someone ends in tears.
cards.gradeReason: Involuntary emotional interruption — everyone freezes, remembering their truth.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: giant eyeball in jar weeping, onion layers dissolved. Mood: involuntary grief.

cards.power: Self-Sabotage. Play on yourself to reroll a failed check.
cards.lore: Man vs. Himself. The interior instability. Can you live with what you have to do? The fundamental drama of being alive.
cards.gradeReason: Reroll your failure — the interior conflict embodied as a mechanical choice.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: man lunging at mirror image, glass shattering. Mood: interior warfare.

cards.power: Sociological Warfare. Force opponent to choose between 2 cards. They lose the unchosen one.
cards.lore: Man vs. Man. My core value is Equality. Yours is Freedom. Now we have to vote. I can't believe who you are.
cards.gradeReason: Force the impossible value-choice — the political drama is the mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: dog in top hat casting vote, burning documents around ballot box. Mood: democracy as combat.

cards.power: Environmental Uprising. Wipe the board. Nature wins.
cards.lore: Man vs. The Elements. The world is indifferent to your "project." We thought we beat nature. We were wrong.
cards.gradeReason: Wipe everything — nature indifferent to human projects. The move is the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: giant tree toppling glass office building, planet watching. Mood: indifferent apocalypse.

cards.power: Cliché Storm. Nullify a unique effect by citing a trope.
cards.lore: Honesty vs. Specificity. You can't have both. That specific agony? That's the generator for ten thousand stories.
cards.gradeReason: Weaponize the cliché — your private agony is also everyone's story.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: skeleton writing the same story endlessly, ten thousand scrolls stacked. Mood: cosmic repetition.

cards.power: Brutal Truth. Deal double damage, but you must reveal your entire hand to the table.
cards.lore: You value the truth. Even if it bleeds your best friend dry. You have to own up to it.
cards.gradeReason: Double damage = full exposure — the cost IS the benefit. Mechanic teaches the ethics.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: shattered face revealing knife, hands open on table, nothing hidden. Mood: devastating honesty.

cards.power: Loyal Dog. Take damage for an ally. Sink with the ship.
cards.lore: I'm a good faithful friend. I'll support you no matter what. Even if you're wrong. Especially if you're wrong.
cards.gradeReason: Sink with the ship — loyalty even unto wrongness. You feel the weight instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: dog standing on tilting ship deck, water rising, unwilling to leave. Mood: noble catastrophe.

cards.power: Forced Choice. Opponent must discard their highest value card.
cards.lore: Push them to the wall. Create a circumstance where they cannot have both values. Watch them squirm.
cards.gradeReason: Force sacrifice of highest value — the whole deck's thesis as one move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: figure pressed against brick wall, two doors that cannot both open. Mood: inescapable dilemma.

cards.power: Abandon Principles. Swap your hand with a discard.
cards.lore: When push comes to shove, something falls by the wayside. You gotta jump. You gotta jump.
cards.gradeReason: Abandon principles to survive — you know the desperation in your bones.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: rat leaping from sinking ship, MORALS sign drowning behind it. Mood: desperate escape.

cards.power: Blunt Force. Ignore defense. Words are short, hard, and old.
cards.lore: I live in a house. Dirt. Wood. Stone. The meat and potatoes. No hiding behind fancy syllables.
cards.gradeReason: Short words as blunt weapon — the lore PERFORMS its mechanic in every syllable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: spiked medieval club forged from dense single-syllable words. Mood: Saxon bluntness.

cards.power: Class Privilege. Nullify a "Blunt Force" attack.
cards.lore: I reside in a mansion. Through the French court, we signal our socioeconomic register. Expensive words for expensive people.
cards.gradeReason: Register as class shield — clever but needs vocabulary awareness to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: 18th-century aristocrat firing eye-laser through monocle, French court attire. Mood: elaborate condescension.

cards.power: Yo! Interrupt an action immediately.
cards.lore: Yo. Give me that. Down and dirty. The signals of who you are and who you think I am.
cards.gradeReason: "Yo!" IS the mechanic — card performs its own power in one syllable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: graffiti megaphone with KINGS tag, immediate urban energy. Mood: raw interruption.

cards.power: Formal Distance. Players cannot attack you for 1 turn.
cards.lore: Will you please pass that? Sending signals to suppress the other person. Distance is a shield.
cards.gradeReason: Formal register as immunity — works well but a beat slower than The Street Register.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: judge in full wig behind glass barrier, untouchable. Mood: institutional immunity.

cards.power: Unbreakable Core. Cannot be destroyed by "Adjective" cards.
cards.lore: The heart and soul. The Predication. Everything else is just decoration. Strip it down.
cards.gradeReason: The core adjectives can't touch — strip to subject+verb. The writer's creed made mechanical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: walnut cracked open, tiny Subject+Verb burning at center. Mood: indestructible truth.

cards.power: Immediate Impact. Attack first in the round. No delay.
cards.lore: He pointed the gun. Boom. Action first, consequence later. Put the shock at the front.
cards.gradeReason: Lead with the gun — lore demonstrates the mechanic in its first sentence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: flintlock pointing forward, smoke trailing behind. Mood: shock first.

cards.power: Withhold Subject. Opponent cannot act until the end of the turn.
cards.lore: Way back, across the yard, near the fence, wait for it... wait for it... She hid.
cards.gradeReason: Grammatical suspense as game-pause — inspired but 'Withhold Subject' takes a moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: dynamite fuse burning toward hidden subject pronoun. Mood: agonizing anticipation.

cards.power: The Interrupt. Cancel an opponent's card as it is being played.
cards.lore: Subject... [chaos/comedy/suspense]... Verb. The rarest form. A key change in the music.
cards.gradeReason: Mid-play interrupt is elegant but 'split predication' is jargon for most players.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: magician slicing sentence in half mid-air, verb and subject separated. Mood: disruptive elegance.

cards.power: Altruism Hack. Force opponent to help you (give you a card).
cards.lore: The Confederate dumps the pencils. If you read the story, you stop to help. Your baseline has shifted.
cards.gradeReason: Story hacks altruism — force help via narrative. The mechanism IS the anecdote.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: scattered pencils on floor, reluctant hand reaching down involuntarily. Mood: involuntary kindness.

cards.power: Voice in Head. Control opponent's next move.
cards.lore: You hear it in your head. The author's voice becomes your voice. Possession by syntax.
cards.gradeReason: Author's voice colonizes opponent — 'possession by syntax' lands instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: inner ear cross-section, tiny author whispering inside. Mood: intimate possession.

cards.power: Forced Identification. Copy the power of the last played card.
cards.lore: Who would I be if I were not myself? The smallest appeal to affect makes people do things logic cannot.
cards.gradeReason: Mirroring mechanic is clear but philosophical lore needs a beat to resonate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: two faces mirroring each other, neural connections glowing between them. Mood: involuntary empathy.

cards.power: Edit History. Retcon a past turn.
cards.lore: I'm a moving target. The reader is a moving target. The world is moving. Give me a red pen.
cards.gradeReason: Retcon a past turn — the writer's perspective on editable reality. Crystal clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: figure running through crosshairs, red pen slashing through past events. Mood: unstoppable revision.

cards.power: Pantheism. Summon a "Nature" card from the deck.
cards.lore: Children know it's alive. Adults say "it's just wood." Recover the animism. Listen to the neighbors.
cards.gradeReason: Animism resonates but 'Nature card' is game-mechanic jargon that needs setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: angry tree with open mouth and eyes, child listening at roots. Mood: recovered animism.

cards.power: Wood Wide Web. Look at everyone's hand.
cards.lore: Brains down there. Root plans. Making problems. Making decisions. We are not alone.
cards.gradeReason: Wood wide web = see all hands — perfect metaphor-to-mechanic fusion.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: brain-like mushroom network underground, roots scanning all hands above. Mood: invisible omniscience.

cards.power: Call the Cavalry. Deal damage equal to the number of cards in your hand.
cards.lore: Send out signals to wasps to save you from attack. The forest takes care of its own.
cards.gradeReason: Bigger hand = harder swarm — the forest-cavalry logic is immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: skull with wasp swarm launching outward from hollow eye. Mood: colony defense.

cards.power: Double Truth. Combine a "Science" card and a "Magic" card for double effect.
cards.lore: Science and Spirit are commensal. Empirical backing for the poetic claim. Know the world both ways.
cards.gradeReason: Science + Magic = double truth — the synthesis of knowing is immediately graspable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: scientist with crystal ball, periodic table merging with star chart. Mood: dual knowing.

cards.power: Specific Shield. Immune to generic attacks.
cards.lore: Not just a tree. An Ash. Diamond-shaped bark. Vivid and distinct.
cards.gradeReason: Specificity = immunity — mechanic teaches the writing lesson in one move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: ash tree with diamond-patterned bark, generic arrows deflecting off. Mood: precise invulnerability.

cards.power: Botanical Strength. +2 to all Attack rolls.
cards.lore: The Ironwood's fluted muscle. See the sinews. Projecting human power onto the wood.
cards.gradeReason: +2 to all attacks — blandest mechanic in the deck for the most specific concept.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: ironwood trunk with visible muscle-like striations, sinews exposed. Mood: silent botanical power.

cards.power: Air Support. Attack any 1 player from any distance.
cards.lore: The Maple's shower of helicopters. Weaponized seeds remembering the seasons of their childhood.
cards.gradeReason: Attack from any distance like weaponized maple seeds — childhood memory as long-range assault.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: maple seeds spiraling in attack-helicopter formation. Mood: weaponized nostalgia.

cards.power: Nostalgia Trip. Revert the game state to the previous turn.
cards.lore: Rockets. Outlandish cars. Mastered areas. The architecture of an 8-year-old's boredom.
cards.gradeReason: Revert via childhood memory — charming but mechanic needs the metaphor to arrive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: child's notebook blueprint of rocket and outlandish car, pencil in foreground. Mood: innocent invention.

cards.power: Deprivation. Ignore all board effects for 1 turn.
cards.lore: Plowing in the dark. Remove the stimuli. Repurpose the sensory apparatus to see the invisible.
cards.gradeReason: Sensory isolation as creative tool — the logic is there but takes a moment to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: figure in flotation tank, external world fading to silence. Mood: chosen blindness.

cards.power: Daily Quota. You must discard 3 cards to stay in the game.
cards.lore: The discipline. Get the words down. Stay there until it's done. A cage of your own making.
cards.gradeReason: Pay to stay in the game — the discipline made punishing. Every writer knows this cage.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: typewriter locked inside birdcage, desk lamp lit, no exit. Mood: productive imprisonment.

cards.power: Horizontal Productivity. Draw 2 cards while resting.
cards.lore: Lying in bed. Covers up. Dictating to the ceiling. Recollecting in tranquility.
cards.gradeReason: Productivity in rest is a lovely paradox — needs writer's-life context to resonate fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: writer in bed dictating to recorder, manuscript pages floating above. Mood: supine genius.

cards.power: Ruthless Edit. Remove a card from play permanently.
cards.lore: Give me another shot at that. You are never done. Slash it. Burn it. Make it effortless.
cards.gradeReason: Permanent removal = ruthless edit. Every writer reaches for this without explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: red pen slashing through blood-red manuscript pages. Mood: savage improvement.

cards.power: Forward Momentum. Advance the game phase.
cards.lore: Language pulls the sled. Diction. Mastery. Syntax. The first dog in the line.
cards.gradeReason: Advance game phase via language momentum — clear but game-mechanic dependent.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: husky in harness labeled LANGUAGE leading a dogsled forward. Mood: driven momentum.

cards.power: Coherence. Link two cards together to share their stats.
cards.lore: All the dogs in harness. Pulling in the same direction. If they pull apart, the story dies.
cards.gradeReason: Link cards = coherence — vivid metaphor but requires knowing the game's link mechanics.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: brain and heart connected by leather harness straps, aligned forward. Mood: disciplined unity.

cards.power: Burden of Plot. Slow an opponent down.
cards.lore: The concern of crafting. The level granular to high level structure. It's heavy.
cards.gradeReason: Slow with plot burden — the weight is felt but the mechanic is one step removed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: enormous manuscript stack as sled being dragged through snow. Mood: exhausting necessity.

cards.power: MFA Rule. Silence a player who talks too much.
cards.lore: Don't spend time telling the scene! Get them doing things! The tyranny of the writing prog[ram]...
cards.gradeReason: Silence the over-explainer — the frustration is universal. You reach for it immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: whip reading SHOW DON'T TELL cracking across word cloud. Mood: impatient authority.

cards.power: Artificial Tension. Force an opponent to engage with you.
cards.lore: Start high. Artificially high. Drop them in before they know what hit them.
cards.gradeReason: Force engagement = the hook. Mechanics of the opening line as card power.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: fishhook through eyeball, narrative line pulled taut. Mood: irresistible capture.

cards.power: Lull. Skip combat for 1 turn.
cards.lore: Relax. Meet the cast. Bait and switch. Once they are oriented, we tighten the screws.
cards.gradeReason: Skip combat for orientation — bait-and-switch strategy needs narrative framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: character lounging in hammock reading, storm clouds massing behind. Mood: false calm.

cards.power: Escalation. Double the stakes of the current challenge.
cards.lore: Every solution creates a larger instability. Up and up. Until you hit the wall.
cards.gradeReason: Double the stakes — escalation as inexorable force. You feel the vertigo instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: ladder extending into storm clouds, each rung catching fire behind it. Mood: relentless ascent.

cards.power: Denouement. Resolve all active effects.
cards.lore: The Knot blows apart. Release the tension. How is the world different now?
cards.gradeReason: Resolve everything at once — the narrative exhale as card. You feel the release.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: Gordian knot exploding outward, all threads releasing simultaneously. Mood: cathartic resolution.

cards.power: Cosmic Perspective. Ignore all "Local" effects.
cards.lore: First there was nothing. Before the litres. Earn the right to tell the local story by starting with the universe.
cards.gradeReason: Cosmic perspective ignores local — earn the intimate by starting with everything.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: Earth as tiny dot in space with 'You are here' arrow. Mood: vertiginous scale.

cards.power: Granularity. Focus damage on a single target.
cards.lore: Look harder. When you are close, look harder. Reality is moving. The detail is the god.
cards.gradeReason: Focus damage = granularity — gorgeous lore but mechanic needs a moment to arrive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: microscope focused on single burning leaf cell. Mood: obsessive precision.

cards.power: The Opener. Play this first to gain Initiative.
cards.lore: The entire book is in a nutshell. Two houses both alike in dignity. The DNA of the drama.
cards.gradeReason: Play first = initiative — opening line as mechanical advantage. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: giant key hovering over book's first page, everything unlocking. Mood: portal opening.

cards.power: Surprise Ending. Swap the values of your Attack and Defense.
cards.lore: Each child's tree has its own... Excellence. Not the word you expected. Play off the AI model in the re[ader]...
cards.gradeReason: Swap attack/defense = subvert expectation — clever but partially truncated lore undercuts landing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: child reading book, expected word replaced mid-page with surprise. Mood: productive disruption.

cards.power: Misunderstanding. Ignore a criticism/attack.
cards.lore: The loneliness of writing. Your brother says "interesting." They don't get it.
cards.gradeReason: Ignore criticism via 'interesting' — writer's loneliness resonates but personally.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: writer handing manuscript to baffled friend surrounded by question marks. Mood: solitary creation.

cards.power: Remote Impact. Affect a player not adjacent to you.
cards.lore: I'm studying forestry because of you. Days later — strangers while you sit in the dark.
cards.gradeReason: Remote impact = changed by a story — true but takes personal connection to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: person in dark room, stranger growing a forest in the distance. Mood: delayed consequence.

cards.power: Re-Entry. Draw 3 cards but take damage.
cards.lore: Plunge back in. Test the products of solitude against the chaos. Get dirty.
cards.gradeReason: Draw 3, take damage — risk/reward of plunging back into chaos. You know the move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: figure diving into whirlpool of social media and city noise. Mood: voluntary chaos.

cards.power: Orbit. Remove yourself from play for 1 turn.
cards.lore: Move in and out of orbit. If you stay solitary, you spin out. If you stay in the world, you disso[lve — text truncated].
cards.gradeReason: Remove self = orbit — the life-cycle of solitude/engagement takes a reflective beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: writer in orbit between isolated cabin and chaotic city. Mood: necessary withdrawal.

cards.power: Silent Movie. Opponents cannot speak for 1 round.
cards.lore: Don't tell me you're angry. Show me the broken glass. (Also, shut up.)
cards.gradeReason: Card silences opponents using the rule itself — performs what it teaches. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: mime in beret standing over broken glass, finger on lips. Mood: enforced demonstration.

cards.power: Purple Prose. Confuse opponent. They miss their turn.
cards.lore: The baroque, fluted, muscular, diamond-shaped, tempestuous verbiage. Too much flavor.
cards.gradeReason: The card IS an adjective overdose — the lore performs the mechanic in real time.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: reader drowning in swirl of adjective word-clouds. Mood: overwhelming excess.

cards.power: Logic Fail. Negate a rule for one turn.
cards.lore: Wait, why did he do that? Who cares. The sled is moving.
cards.gradeReason: Negate a rule — 'Who cares, the sled is moving.' Perfect anarchic permission.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: burning hole in narrative map, sled racing cheerfully past. Mood: joyful incoherence.

cards.power: Lazy Fix. Win a tie automatically.
cards.lore: God from the machine. When you can't untie the knot, just cut it.
cards.gradeReason: Win the tie with a lazy fix — everyone knows this shameless move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: giant mechanical hand descending to cut tangled plot threads. Mood: shameless rescue.

cards.lore: Draw your own Kayfabizarro Kards.
cards.gradeReason: Meta-invitation — you know what to do but it's not a performative card per se.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: blank card frame with pencil, open invitation to create. Mood: pure potential.

cards.power: Instruction.
cards.lore: 1. Print. 2. Cut. 3. Play. 4. Lie about the rules. 5. Stay Fluffy.
cards.gradeReason: Rules as card — delightful meta-framing but not a performance card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: scissors cutting card border, FrizzleBob winking alongside step list. Mood: anarchic instruction.

cards.power: The Mascot. Use as a Wild Card.
cards.lore: Analog-first DIY cut & play artist. Epistemic sabotage. Layout anarchist.
cards.gradeReason: Wild card — you know exactly who he is and what to do with him.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit mascot arms spread wide, chaotic creative energy. Mood: anarchic charm.

cards.power: The Objective. Push them to the wall. Make them choose. If they don't cry, you aren't writing hard enough.
cards.lore: Push them to the wall. Make them choose. If they don't cry, you aren't writing hard enough.
cards.gradeReason: The whole deck's thesis in one card — devastating clarity, zero explanation required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink wash, parchment. Subject: PUSH THEM in giant letters on brick wall, cornered figure choosing. Mood: devastating imperative.

verdict: Pulitzer Punk is the writer's brain dissected and laid out as a card game — The Honesty Shiv's double-damage-for-full-disclosure is mechanic-as-ethics, and The Golden Rule closing the deck is a gut punch you cannot ignore. Named strength: The Wall / Honesty Shiv / Ballot Box triptych — three cards that together stage the entire honesty-vs-fidelity conflict without a single explanation needed. Named weakness: The Fluted Muscle is a +2 attack bonus hiding inside one of the most evocative concepts in the deck; the Ironwood's sinews deserve a sharper move. Table-ready Y.
blurb: For writers, journalists, and anyone who's ever had to choose between the truth and loyalty — 60 cards that put your characters through the wall and dare them to come out crying.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: PULITZER PUNK – Truth or Loyalty, Pick One and Bleed (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Do you love your characters too much to write them well?

Here is the instinct that keeps your best pages safe and dead. The second a scene starts to hurt, you flinch. You hand the character an out. You let them keep their dignity, their secret, their excuse, and you call it kindness. It is not kindness. It is the loyalty you owe a real person, smuggled onto the page where it has no business being. Most flat drafts do not die of bad ideas. They die of mercy.

PULITZER PUNK is Social Story Wrestling for the writer who has gone soft on their own cast. Sixty cut-and-play cards you throw at a character out loud, while the table decides whether they break honestly or wriggle off the hook. Half of them are pressure. The other half are the cheap exits you reach for the moment the pressure starts to work.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Pulitzer Punk Core Deck: 60 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Wall (you do not write around it, you write the character straight into it and report what comes out), The Honesty Shiv (the one true line they would do anything not to say, so you make them say it), and The 10,000 Stories (every life holds ten thousand versions, and the one you pick is a confession about you).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No spreadsheets, no math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and Cut & Cheat permission to break your own scene on purpose.
- The Honesty-versus-Fidelity Engine: The Plot Hole that opens right under the lie you were protecting, plus Uncle FrizzleBob's Golden Rule stamped on the last page, if it breaks fix it, if it's missing add it, then destroy this book.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
By grabbing this deck, you aren't just buying a static PDF. You are entering the Protopian Pipeline. All future thematic expansions and topic-specific decks in this cycle are included as FREE updates for you.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
The page is the one room left where you can tell the truth about people and call it a story. I make these to keep that room open. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Use it. Put your characters through the wall. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes into the time I spend drawing and writing the next cards.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"A character you refuse to hurt is a character you refuse to know."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
